soundness_flags.label: def:representation-distance; def:quotient-confidence-set; thm:quotient-confidence-set
soundness_flags.one_line: The declared representation “pseudometric” is directed because it integrates only against \(\bar P_\theta\), so the confidence-set diameter is undefined without a symmetrized or explicitly directed metric convention.

soundness_flags.label: ass:smoothness-order
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited quantitative-Morse theorem assumes \(k\ge3\), whereas this standard-tagged condition allows \(k=2\); the citation does not support the tag as stated.

soundness_flags.label: ass:critical-order
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited quantitative-Morse theorem produces nondegenerate Morse critical points after perturbation and does not support the asserted arbitrary finite-order index \(1\le m\le k-1\).

soundness_flags.label: ass:decoder-smoothness; ass:decoder-conditioning
soundness_flags.one_line: CauCA’s exact-identification setup uses differentiable invertible transformations and interventional discrepancy, not the uniform \(C^k\) and bi-Lipschitz envelopes that load the proposed rate; retag and independently justify these strengthened rate assumptions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes an almost-everywhere derivative discrepancy and proves exact identifiability under single-node stochastic interventions; its stated transformation ambiguity is through C1 diffeomorphisms, not a uniform bounded C^k/bi-Lipschitz rate class.
Two coupled hard interventions with discrepancy identify a node up to a diffeomorphism; with observational data they identify the latent DAG and variables up to componentwise diffeomorphisms.

The paper studies approximate nonlinear representation learning under mixing close to a local isometry and invokes rigidity-based approximate recovery; it is not a complete-interventional-law modulus result.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1 abstract; pp. 7 and 9, Theorem 1 and conclusion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The finite-sample result uses stochastic soft interventions and an unknown linear transformation, with partial graph/latent recovery; it leaves general transformations and hard-intervention perfect identification as future work.
The theorem fixes \(k\ge3\) and constructs a perturbation whose critical points are nondegenerate, separated, and finite; it does not state a general finite-order \(m\)-critical-profile condition.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a symmetric quotient metric, for example by using \(\frac12(\bar P_\theta+\bar P_{\widetilde\theta})\) or the maximum of both directed losses, and restate confidence-set diameter using that metric.

Retag the uniform \(C^k\), conditioning, and finite-order assumptions as novel rate conditions, give a concrete circular-mechanism/decoder application that satisfies them, and separate the \(k=2\) Morse case from citations requiring \(k\ge3\).

Add a theorem-level comparison showing exactly which published exact-identification hypotheses are strictly weakened or retained, rather than leaving the stability theorem merely informed by several exact results.

recommended_next_step: Revise the metric and assumption provenance first; the field-tier causal stability kernel is novel on both checked axes once those statement-level defects are repaired.
